doc.title: Phil Woods — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The seventies peak
summary: Grammys, Tom Harrell and Hal Galper, and good health.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Being honored: NEA Jazz Masters and other awards

blocks.x: So, in the seventies you won Grammy for Images, won a Grammy for Showboat …
… You have a group that’s steadily working. Are you doing what you want to do?
Can you call the shots a lot more than you ever had in your career?

Oh yeah that was a great period, especially the band with Tom Harrell and Hal Galper, I think, was probably the … Well, I think they’ve all been good bands but I really liked that period. We were all in our prime I think, you know. I hadn’t been hit with my pulmonary problems, the lungs were still good, I still had

my original teeth and so you know, I felt really good about playing. It gets a little harder as you get older, you know. But I think that’s really some good stuff when I listen to it. I like most of the stuff we played. I think it retains a certain level of expertise and music we recorded I’m not ashamed of anything. [telephone rings] Want to grab that?
So you’ve got this band, and you’re, in other words, you can kind of pick and choose. Your popularity’s going up pretty good …
We were busy, very busy. We could call our own shots, yeah.
